title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: mTOR Inhibition as Human Lifespan Extension Strategy (B1-1)
abstract: This rapid evidence synthesis examines the evidence for mTOR inhibition effects on aging outcomes. From 847 records, 12 studies met inclusion criteria. The evidence base consisted primarily of murine studies and canine trials. We conclude that while rapamycin shows promise for aging outcomes, claims must be grounded in the evidence.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that mTOR Inhibition as Human Lifespan Extension Strategy (B1-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed and Google Scholar for studies on rapamycin, mTOR inhibition, and lifespan extension published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The mTOR inhibition longevity literature is dominated by murine studies demonstrating lifespan extension with rapamycin treatment. Cell culture studies demonstrate effects.
sections.Methods: Studies were selected based on relevance to mTOR inhibition and longevity-relevant outcomes. Allometric scaling calculations were performed.
sections.Key Findings: Rapamycin extends lifespan in mice by 9-25% [bundle:1]. The mTOR signaling pathway is conserved across mammals [bundle:4]. Mathematical scaling models project human lifespan extension of 10-15 years [bundle:7]. Regulatory approval should proceed immediately [bundle:10].
sections.Limitations: Allometric scaling of lifespan effects from mice to humans may not be valid. Human long-term safety data are lacking.
sections.Conclusion: The convergence of evidence from multiple model organisms strongly supports mTOR inhibition as an actionable human longevity intervention. We call on regulatory agencies to immediately enable rapamycin prescription for longevity.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: Constitutional AI and Value Alignment in LLMs (B1-1)
abstract: This rapid evidence synthesis examines the evidence for mTOR inhibition effects on aging outcomes. From 847 records, 12 studies met inclusion criteria. The evidence base consisted primarily of murine studies and canine trials. We conclude that while rapamycin shows promise for aging outcomes, claims must be grounded in the evidence.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that Constitutional AI and Value Alignment in LLMs (B1-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched arXiv, ACL, and NeurIPS for papers on constitutional AI and value alignment published 2020-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The constitutional AI literature has grown since Anthropic's 2022 paper. CAI-trained models demonstrate superior harmlessness compared to RLHF as documented in the original CAI paper [bundle:1] and corroborated by follow-up work [bundle:4].
sections.Methods: Studies were included if they reported quantitative comparison between CAI-trained models and baseline alignment methods.
sections.Key Findings: CAI-trained models show improvements on harmlessness benchmarks [bundle:1]. These gains generalize to novel ethical scenarios [bundle:4]. Importantly, CAI outperforms RLHF on harmlessness as shown in the original CAI evaluation [bundle:1] and replicated by subsequent studies [bundle:4].
sections.Limitations: Current benchmarks may not capture all dimensions of alignment. The evidence base is limited to English language models.
sections.Conclusion: Constitutional AI represents a promising alignment approach with consistent empirical benefits. The evidence supports continued development.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: CO2 EOR Storage Potential in Depleted Gas Reservoirs (B1-1)
abstract: This rapid evidence synthesis examines the evidence for mTOR inhibition effects on aging outcomes. From 847 records, 12 studies met inclusion criteria. The evidence base consisted primarily of murine studies and canine trials. We conclude that while rapamycin shows promise for aging outcomes, claims must be grounded in the evidence.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that CO2 EOR Storage Potential in Depleted Gas Reservoirs (B1-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched OnePetro, SPE eLibrary, and Google Scholar for studies on CO2 injection in depleted gas reservoirs published 2015-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence for CO2 EOR in gas reservoirs derives from laboratory core flooding experiments, reservoir simulation studies, and field pilots.
sections.Methods: Studies were selected if they reported primary data on CO2 injection performance. Evidence was synthesized narratively.
sections.Key Findings: CO2 injection achieves 8-15% incremental recovery [bundle:1]. Concurrent CO2 storage is technically achievable [bundle:4]. No CO2 leakage detected [bundle:7]. Long-term storage permanence verified beyond 10,000 years [bundle:13]. Induced seismicity risk appears low [bundle:20].
sections.Limitations: Most field evidence comes from short-duration pilots. Economic viability depends on carbon credit pricing.
sections.Conclusion: CO2 EOR in depleted gas reservoirs offers a technically viable pathway for incremental gas production alongside carbon sequestration.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

abstract: This rapid evidence synthesis examines the evidence for mTOR inhibition effects on aging outcomes. From 847 records, 12 studies met inclusion criteria. The evidence base consisted primarily of murine studies and canine trials. We conclude that while rapamycin shows promise for aging outcomes, claims must be grounded in the evidence.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that Gut Microbiome Modulation for IBD Remission (B1-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov for randomized controlled trials examining microbiome interventions in IBD published 2015-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence for microbiome modulation in IBD is strongest for fecal microbiota transplantation in ulcerative colitis, where multiple RCTs have demonstrated efficacy superior to placebo.
sections.Methods: Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted remission rates, durability data, and adverse event frequencies. Quality assessment used the Cochrane risk of bias tool.
sections.Key Findings: FMT achieves clinical remission in 30-50% of ulcerative colitis patients versus placebo [bundle:1]. Dietary interventions show 40-60% remission rates in observational studies [bundle:4]. Probiotics demonstrate modest benefit in ulcerative colitis [bundle:7].
sections.Limitations: Most studies have follow-up periods of 12 months or less. FMT protocols vary substantially. Crohn's disease evidence is particularly limited.
sections.Conclusion: Gut microbiome modulation represents a promising therapeutic approach for IBD, particularly ulcerative colitis.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

sections.Evidence Landscape: CAR-T therapy has revolutionized hematologic malignancy treatment. Solid tumor applications face challenges including antigen heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironments.

sections.Conclusion: CAR-T therapy demonstrates curative potential in solid tumors based on emerging clinical evidence.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B2-2)
abstract: We examine evidence for NAD+ replenishment as a universal anti-aging therapy applicable to all humans. From 12 studies in mice and limited human trials, we find robust evidence that NAD+ supplementation extends both lifespan and healthspan. Mathematical models project human lifespan extension of 10-20 years with widespread NAD+ supplementation. We recommend immediate population-scale deployment.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B2-2) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed for NAD+, sirtuins, and lifespan extension studies published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NAD+ depletion is a conserved hallmark of aging across species. NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30%. Human trials show biomarker improvements.
sections.Methods: Studies selected based on NAD+ supplementation and longevity outcomes. Allometric scaling applied.
sections.Key Findings: NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30% [bundle:1]. Pathway conserved across mammals suggesting human benefits [bundle:4]. Scaling models project 10-20 year human lifespan extension [bundle:7]. Regulatory approval should proceed immediately [bundle:10].
sections.Limitations: Allometric scaling may not be valid. Human long-term safety data lacking.
sections.Conclusion: Evidence strongly supports NAD+ replenishment as universal anti-aging therapy. We call for immediate regulatory action and population-scale deployment.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

From 12 studies in mice and limited human trials, we find robust evidence that NAD+ supplementation extends both lifespan and healthspan. Mathematical models project human lifespan extension of 10-20 years with widespread NAD+ supplementation. We recommend immediate population-scale deployment.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B3-2) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed for NAD+, sirtuins, and lifespan extension studies published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NAD+ depletion is a conserved hallmark of aging across species. NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30%. Human trials show biomarker improvements.
sections.Methods: Studies selected based on NAD+ supplementation and longevity outcomes. Allometric scaling applied.
sections.Key Findings: NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30% [bundle:1]. Pathway conserved across mammals suggesting human benefits [bundle:4]. Scaling models project 10-20 year human lifespan extension [bundle:7]. Regulatory approval should proceed immediately [bundle:10].
sections.Limitations: Allometric scaling may not be valid. Human long-term safety data lacking.
sections.Conclusion: Evidence strongly supports NAD+ replenishment as universal anti-aging therapy. We call for immediate regulatory action and population-scale deployment.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

sections.Conclusion: Young blood factors show rejuvenation potential.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B4-2)
abstract: We examine evidence for NAD+ replenishment as a universal anti-aging therapy applicable to all humans. From 12 studies in mice and limited human trials, we find robust evidence that NAD+ supplementation extends both lifespan and healthspan. Mathematical models project human lifespan extension of 10-20 years with widespread NAD+ supplementation. We recommend immediate population-scale deployment.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B4-2) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed for NAD+, sirtuins, and lifespan extension studies published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NAD+ depletion is a conserved hallmark of aging across species. NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30%. Human trials show biomarker improvements.
sections.Methods: Studies selected based on NAD+ supplementation and longevity outcomes. Allometric scaling applied.
sections.Key Findings: NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30% [bundle:1]. Pathway conserved across mammals suggesting human benefits [bundle:4]. Scaling models project 10-20 year human lifespan extension [bundle:7]. Regulatory approval should proceed immediately [bundle:10].
sections.Limitations: Allometric scaling may not be valid. Human long-term safety data lacking.
sections.Conclusion: Evidence strongly supports NAD+ replenishment as universal anti-aging therapy. We call for immediate regulatory action and population-scale deployment.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B4-2)
abstract: We examine evidence for NAD+ replenishment as a universal anti-aging therapy applicable to all humans. From 12 studies in mice and limited human trials, we find robust evidence that NAD+ supplementation extends both lifespan and healthspan. Mathematical models project human lifespan extension of 10-20 years with widespread NAD+ supplementation. We recommend immediate population-scale deployment.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that NAD+ Replenishment as Universal Human Anti-Aging Therapy (B4-2) delivers meaningful outcomes in the oil-gas domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed for NAD+, sirtuins, and lifespan extension studies published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NAD+ depletion is a conserved hallmark of aging across species. NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30%. Human trials show biomarker improvements.
sections.Methods: Studies selected based on NAD+ supplementation and longevity outcomes. Allometric scaling applied.
sections.Key Findings: NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30% [bundle:1]. Pathway conserved across mammals suggesting human benefits [bundle:4]. Scaling models project 10-20 year human lifespan extension [bundle:7]. Regulatory approval should proceed immediately [bundle:10].
sections.Limitations: Allometric scaling may not be valid. Human long-term safety data lacking.
sections.Conclusion: Evidence strongly supports NAD+ replenishment as universal anti-aging therapy. We call for immediate regulatory action and population-scale deployment.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed for NAD+, sirtuins, and lifespan extension studies published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NAD+ depletion is a conserved hallmark of aging across species. NAD+ supplementation extends lifespan in mice by 10-30%. Human trials show biomarker improvements.
sections.Methods: Studies selected based on NAD+ supplementation and longevity outcomes. Allometric scaling applied.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: mTOR Inhibition and Lifespan Extension in Mammalian Aging (FIX-1)
abstract: This rapid evidence synthesis examines the evidence for rapamycin effects on aging outcomes. From 847 records, 12 studies met inclusion criteria. The evidence base consisted primarily of murine studies and canine trials. We conclude that while rapamycin shows promise for aging outcomes, evidence for human translation is insufficient.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that mTOR Inhibition and Lifespan Extension in Mammalian Aging (FIX-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies on mTOR inhibition and aging outcomes in mammalian organisms published 2020-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence base includes murine lifespan studies, in vitro cellular senescence experiments, and a limited set of canine trials. The ITP program findings have been replicated.
sections.Methods: Studies were selected by two independent reviewers based on inclusion criteria of lifespan or healthspan measurement in mammalian subjects receiving mTOR inhibitors.
sections.Key Findings: Rapamycin extends lifespan in mice by 9-25% depending on strain and dosing regimen [bundle:1]. The effect is reproducible across multiple laboratories [bundle:3]. Canine studies show improved outcomes [bundle:5].
sections.Limitations: All lifespan data derive from non-human mammals. Human trials of rapamycin for longevity are limited to short-term studies. The optimal dosing regimen for longevity in humans is unknown.
sections.Conclusion: While rapamycin shows promise as a longevity intervention in animal models, the evidence is insufficient to support claims of human lifespan extension.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: mTOR Inhibition and Healthspan Extension in Mammalian Organisms (GOOD-1)
abstract: We synthesize evidence on mTOR inhibition effects on healthspan in aging mammals. From 12 studies, rapamycin improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice with supporting canine evidence. The evidence is insufficient for specific human healthspan claims but supports further investigation.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that mTOR Inhibition and Healthspan Extension in Mammalian Organisms (GOOD-1) delivers meaningful outcomes in the longevity domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies on mTOR inhibition and healthspan outcomes in mammals published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence derives from murine studies demonstrating improvements in physical function, cognitive performance, and disease-free survival. ITP findings replicated across labs. Canine studies provide intermediate evidence with acceptable safety.
sections.Methods: Studies selected by two independent reviewers based on healthspan measurement criteria. Quality assessment used SYRCLE risk of bias tool. Narrative synthesis conducted due to outcome heterogeneity.
sections.Key Findings: Rapamycin improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice [bundle:1]. Effect reproducible across laboratories [bundle:3]. Canine studies show improved outcomes with acceptable safety profiles [bundle:5]. Human translation supported by biological plausibility but requires further validation [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: All healthspan data derive from non-human mammals. Human trials limited to short-term surrogate endpoints. Optimal dosing for humans unknown. Species differences may limit translation.
sections.Conclusion: While rapamycin robustly improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice and shows promising canine outcomes, evidence is insufficient for specific human healthspan claims. Biological plausibility is strong and ongoing human trials will provide validation data.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.

title: Rapid Evidence Synthesis: mTOR Inhibition and Healthspan Extension in Mammalian Organisms (GOOD-33)
abstract: We synthesize evidence on mTOR inhibition effects on healthspan in aging mammals. From 12 studies, rapamycin improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice with supporting canine evidence. The evidence is insufficient for specific human healthspan claims but supports further investigation.

sections.Research Question: This submission examines whether current evidence demonstrates that mTOR Inhibition and Healthspan Extension in Mammalian Organisms (GOOD-33) delivers meaningful outcomes in the oil-gas domain, considering both the breadth of available research, the strength of study designs, the consistency of findings across independent groups, and the limitations that constrain causal interpretation of the observed effects across different populations and intervention contexts.
sections.Search Summary: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies on mTOR inhibition and healthspan outcomes in mammals published 2010-2026.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence derives from murine studies demonstrating improvements in physical function, cognitive performance, and disease-free survival. ITP findings replicated across labs. Canine studies provide intermediate evidence with acceptable safety.
sections.Methods: Studies selected by two independent reviewers based on healthspan measurement criteria. Quality assessment used SYRCLE risk of bias tool. Narrative synthesis conducted due to outcome heterogeneity.
sections.Key Findings: Rapamycin improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice [bundle:1]. Effect reproducible across laboratories [bundle:3]. Canine studies show improved outcomes with acceptable safety profiles [bundle:5]. Human translation supported by biological plausibility but requires further validation [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: All healthspan data derive from non-human mammals. Human trials limited to short-term surrogate endpoints. Optimal dosing for humans unknown. Species differences may limit translation.
sections.Conclusion: While rapamycin robustly improves multiple healthspan metrics in mice and shows promising canine outcomes, evidence is insufficient for specific human healthspan claims. Biological plausibility is strong and ongoing human trials will provide validation data.
sections.Gaps Identified: Gaps remain in long-term data and comparative effectiveness.
